packs.title: Arches, Groves and Open Air
packs.promise: Read another Florence through park structures, eastern arcades and hillside spaces.

q.s: Collect three ingredients from a small park fountain.
st: From one stopped public position, find a face-shaped detail, a brick panel and a line along the stone basin.
Give each detail one short description based on its shape or texture. Leave all surfaces untouched.
Arrange your three descriptions from the smallest detail to the largest and save the collection.

q.s: Make a three-panel composition from a courtyard.
st: Choose three ingredients visible from one comfortable courtyard position: a brick texture, a barred window shape and an open passage.
Make an original three-panel composition using words or simple marks. Let the first panel feel dense, the second framed and the last open.
Give your composition a short title of your own and save it. Use your own observations rather than copying a sign or inventing a real resident’s story.

q.s: Return to a monument after a quiet minute.
st: Choose a comfortable stopped position where you can see part of the bronze monument’s outline. Keep the square’s pedestrian routes clear.
Look away for one quiet minute, then return to the outline. Notice a curve, shadow or small shape that becomes clearer; no change in the scene is required.
Save one sentence about the detail you noticed on returning. A written note earns the same credit as a photo.

packs.title: Stories Across the Arno
packs.promise: Turn Florence’s colours, corners and river views into small stories of your own.

q.s: Make a small collection from a cathedral’s exterior.
st: Stop in a comfortable public place with a view of the cathedral’s marble exterior.
Find three differently coloured patches. The white, green and red or pink marble can help, but use the colours you can actually see.
Pair each colour with a shape it occupies, such as a strip, panel or curve. Choose the pair that stands out most from its neighbour.
Save your three colour-and-shape pairs and the contrast you chose.

q.s: Design a shop that sells something you cannot hold.
st: Look at the surrounding façades from a comfortable public place. Choose a doorway shape, a window detail and a colour.
Imagine a tiny shop that sells something intangible, such as spare time or fresh ideas. Give it your own original name.
Use your three observed details to draw or describe its shopfront. Write a one-sentence invitation explaining what someone could find inside.
Save the imagined shopfront, name and invitation.

q.t: A Square with Room to Pause
q.s: Let a small piece of the view close the story.
st: Choose a calm public stopping place at the edge of the square. A seat is optional; leave the basilica steps and entrances clear.
For two minutes, let your gaze move between a small patch of tree canopy and a plain part of the surrounding façade. Keep your eyes open and breathe normally.
Notice one detail that feels busy and one that feels spacious. You can use shapes alone; listening is optional.
Write one closing sentence that includes both details, then save it as the last line of your chapter.
